title: Metal lowering declares threadgroup memory the pipeline dead-code-eliminates for multi-SIMD-group elementwise kernels

evidence.note: run_fault harness_fault at environment stage, turn 1: 'Metal archive helper observations differ from the admitted pipeline'; 2,370,740 provider tokens burned
candidate lowering with 1024 lanes (32 SIMD groups), purely elementwise body; line 17 declares 'threadgroup float share[32]' which the body never references
compiled pipeline reports static_threadgroup_memory_bytes=0 (allocation eliminated) while the declared toolchain requirements said 128 bytes
recurrence on a second workload, same fault string, turn 1: run_fault harness_fault 'Metal archive helper observations differ from the admitted pipeline'
line 18 declares 'threadgroup float share[8]' (32 bytes) which the elementwise body never references
compiled pipeline reports static_threadgroup_memory_bytes=0 against the 32-byte declaration - same declared!=observed XOR refusal at a different share size

observation: src/open_cake_ir/compiler/backends/metal.py:359-366 emits 'threadgroup float share[N]' unconditionally whenever SIMD groups > 1, and lab/metal_build.py:201 forces (>32 threads iff threadgroup memory declared). A purely elementwise multi-group kernel therefore declares bytes it never uses; the Metal compiler eliminates the unused allocation, the sealed archive's pipeline observation reports 0, and the strict declared==observed check at lab/metal_build.py:68-71 raises a campaign-fatal harness_fault on a semantically harmless candidate. Recurs across workloads: silu (32 groups, 128 bytes) and swiglu (8 floats, 32 bytes) both produced multi-SIMD elementwise candidates the model author chose freely - this is a recurring authoring pattern, not a one-task accident.
proposed_change: Emit share[] only when the schedule actually lowers a cross-SIMD-group collective through threadgroup memory, and report threadgroup_memory_bytes from that same fact. Decouple the threads/tgmem XOR rule so a 1024-thread elementwise kernel may declare zero. Keep the declared==observed strictness in the validator unchanged - the declaration should become truthful, not the check looser.
verified_by: Replay rather than campaign, because the failure was a static declaration mismatch. tests/contracts/test_metal.py asserts both directions at once: a four-group purely elementwise kernel now declares zero threadgroup bytes and emits no `share` symbol, and a four-group reduction at the same shape still declares its sixteen -- so the fix narrowed the declaration rather than removing it. The full canonical Corpus Gate ran 124/124 over 174 sources with no expectation regenerated, and refresh_corpus_expectations.py reports the pinned lowerings already match, which establishes that no existing emitted source moved. The cited silu and swiglu campaign workspaces were not re-run, so what is verified is the declaration and the corpus, not those two runs. The regression test does not execute the kernel: the portable CPU shim models a single SIMD group and cannot run a multi-group body.
verification_plan: Bug-fix tick, replay-verified: re-lower the exact candidate sources retained in the silu-20260909c and swiglu-20260910 workspaces under the successor Executor/Compiler revision; the same builds must pass pipeline admission.
